completion:
Request clarification where the record is absent or vague.
3. Come up with a proper description, including a sketch.
4. Consult the basis of design if available.
5. Synthesize a proper action to correct the fault.
6. Update the records and so on.

'When it failed to collect accurate data about what was found to be wrong, and exactly what must be done to correct those faults, a picture of the true trouble spot area remained unnecessarily vague'¹. The writer and her associates used the phrase 'Face the Problem' at the beginning of this article. The necessary first step is a proper boundary line between real (or acceptable) faults against result-irrelevant items, such as the rusty look of a sprinkler head, mostly a cosmetic item.
